race: Formula 1 MSC Cruises Grande Prêmio de São Paulo 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to the Race Weekend Podcast, and São Paulo is the first real punch in the next title war, so bring your coffee.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: It is the first page of the next championship battle, and the BBC has all the coverage details for the weekend from six to eight November.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Perfect timing, because this is not a filler date, this is a statement date for the whole grid, and everyone is watching.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Antonelli says twenty seven preparation starts now, and the boy from Bologna became world champion, so the story is still building.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The title win is the beginning of something special, and that is the tone for Mercedes in Brazil, with confidence high and the pressure real.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Russell says he will take a deep, deep look in the mirror, which is a very British way to say no excuses and full focus.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Ferrari has the Hamilton and Leclerc problem, which is a good problem if you can actually solve it in one weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The how to follow details are out, so everyone can track the action, and that is perfect for a weekend this big.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So let us start with our top pick, Kimi Antonelli, and I am high confidence because he is champion, dominant, and strong at São Paulo.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His history at this circuit is clean, average finish second, best finish second, and one podium in one race, which is exactly the right proof.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is not a lot of races, but it is the right kind of evidence, he arrives with momentum and a car that can win, and the team is ready.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: How do you beat that in a place where he already looks comfortable on Sunday?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: You bring Max Verstappen, and that is the second pick, high confidence because he is the circuit ace, has recent wins, and is a real championship threat.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His history here is scary, average finish of one point seven, best finish first, three podiums in three races, and that is not a fluke.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Wait, one point seven, does that mean he is basically always on the podium every single time?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Average finish of one point seven means he has been winning or near winning, and he still has championship threat, so we cannot ignore him.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the man, but I still like Lewis Hamilton for the third pick because his recent form is strong and the car is finding speed.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Ferrari pace is real, and if the car finds the right balance, he can be right in the mix, maybe even ahead of Max.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I am not buying it, his history here is average finish ninth, best finish eighth, zero podiums in two races, and history is a loud voice.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Easy to say now, but the form is there, and if Ferrari sort the problem, he is a podium threat, maybe even a win threat, because the fans will love it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Charles Leclerc is the fourth pick because he is consistent with Ferrari and has podiums, and that is a big deal when the team is this close.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now for the deep cut, and I want to talk about the one low confidence pick that could embarrass us, and it might sting.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Pierre Gasly is the tenth pick, low confidence, but his circuit history and mid pack points make him the one to watch all weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: If Alpine find the front wing magic, he is the upset of the weekend, and I love that gamble against the big names, and the data supports it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lando Norris is the fifth pick because recent top fives and past São Paulo wins keep him close, and George Russell is the sixth pick with solid pace and a historical fourth here.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Isack Hadjar is the seventh pick for consistent points, Lawson is the eighth pick for reliable points and recent top sevens, and Piastri is the ninth pick for pace.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So the full top ten is Antonelli, Verstappen, Hamilton, Leclerc, Norris, Russell, Hadjar, Lawson, Piastri, Gasly, and that is our São Paulo preview, now enjoy the show.
